solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Most of novel set in which isle?

indicators.note: 'set in' tells us one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: 'which' as a relative pronoun can be replaced by 'that'

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its final letter, so the last one is dropped

parts.note: novel means new

explanation.surface: A quiz question asking which island provides the setting for most of a certain novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops a final letter and 'set in' signals insertion. Thanet is a former island at the eastern tip of Kent, still called the Isle of Thanet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Thanet is the traditional name for this corner of Kent, once separated from the mainland by a channel.

clue.text: Easy … don't panic! Keep calm!

indicators.note: to panic is to flap about wildly, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A string of soothing exclamations, the kind of thing said to someone on the verge of losing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don't panic!' reads as reassurance, but 'panic' is the anagram signal working on EASY and DONT; the apostrophe gives no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a British exclamation urging restraint, equivalent to a command to stay composed.

clue.text: Rochester's missile launching site

indicators.note: the 's reads as 'has', so the city's name has the answer held within its letters

explanation.surface: Pointing to the spot in the Kent city of Rochester from which a rocket or missile is fired.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit within rOCHEster. The 'missile' is a dart, which is why the definition is a playful overstatement.
explanation.definitionFit: In darts the line behind which a player stands to throw is called by this name, so it is where the small missiles are launched.

clue.text: City club perhaps dodgy (closing early)

parts.note: a club is one example of a playing card, from the suit of clubs

indicators.note: closing early means the word stops before its last letter

parts.note: dodgy means iffy, doubtful

explanation.surface: A city nightclub that seems a bit dubious and shuts its doors before the advertised time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks club as an example of a card. 'closing early' cuts IFFY to IFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardiff is the capital city of Wales.

clue.text: Forcibly speak with driver over scrape

indicators.note: in a down entry, 'over' puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: Jenson Button is a British Formula One racing driver, world champion in 2009
a scrape is a shallow hole scratched in the ground

explanation.surface: Accosting a motorist who has had a minor bump or scratched the car.
explanation.walkthrough: Jenson Button, the British Formula One champion, is the driver. 'over' places his name above HOLE in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To detain someone and talk at them insistently, catching hold of them as if by the coat lapel, is this verb.

clue.text: Constant failure, one concludes

parts.note: C is the standard symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
a failure, an unsuccessful person, is a loser

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps failing finally reaches a conclusion about themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: C for a constant is a scientific convention, as with the speed of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Something or someone that brings an event to an end, like a final act or item on a programme, is a closer.

clue.text: Girl singer Jones made tougher

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name
Aled Jones is a Welsh singer, famous as a boy soprano

explanation.surface: A young woman and a Welsh singer named Jones were made more resilient by something.
explanation.walkthrough: Aled Jones became famous as a boy soprano for 'Walking in the Air'.
explanation.definitionFit: Annealing heats and slowly cools metal or glass to make it stronger and less brittle.

clue.text: I didn't hear inventor speaking

indicators.note: speaking says the word is to be heard rather than read, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: James Watt was the Scottish inventor who improved the steam engine

explanation.surface: Someone admits they missed what an inventor said during a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: James Watt, the steam-engine pioneer, said out loud matches the interjection asking someone to repeat themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Said on its own as a question, this word asks for something to be repeated because the listener missed it.

clue.text: Old film star's taking you abroad to Spain — hopefully it might lead to intimacy

definitions.text: hopefully it might lead to intimacy

indicators.note: taking means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Charlie Chaplin was a star of silent films
tu is French for you
E is the international vehicle registration for Spain

explanation.surface: An old movie star whisks you off to Spain, hoping it leads to romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' puts TU (French 'you') into CHAPLIN; E, Spain's car code, ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: A flirtatious opening remark used to start a conversation with someone you fancy, in the hope of romance.

clue.text: Packed as a precaution

definitions.meaning: packed away inside a box or container

explanation.surface: Someone has packed something extra, just to be safe.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is literal, put inside a container; the other is the idiom for being prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase means stored inside a container; as an idiom it means to guard against a possibility.

clue.text: Gripping audition TV judge hated

indicators.note: gripping means holding, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: Judge John Deed was a BBC television drama series starring Martin Shaw
an audition is a test of a performer

explanation.surface: A tense talent-show audition, and the panel judge loathed the act.
explanation.walkthrough: Judge John Deed was a BBC drama about a High Court judge; 'Gripping' has DEED hold TEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Detested and hated are synonyms, both meaning loathed intensely.

clue.text: Another failure with Tyrus? No, not my responsibility!

indicators.note: another version of these letters means a rearrangement of them

explanation.surface: The setter, Tyrus, imagines a solver groaning at yet another failed puzzle and disowning it.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram pool is FAILURE, TYRUS and NO, with 'Another' as the signal; Tyrus is the setter's own pseudonym.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom tells someone that the consequences of their decision are theirs alone to bear.

clue.text: Run-down crappy cafe — round side for admittance

indicators.note: crappy means badly made, so these letters are knocked into a new shape
the side of the word for is its last letter, at its edge

explanation.surface: A shabby greasy-spoon cafe, where you have to go round the side to get in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crappy' is the anagram signal; 'side' points at the edge letter of 'for', and 'admittance' just completes the picture of going in by the side door.
explanation.definitionFit: A neglected, run-down building is one that nobody has looked after.

clue.text: Live right by lovely woman

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist
lovely means nice

explanation.surface: Someone chooses to live close to a beautiful woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Bernice is a female given name, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: National support at the outset — what Cameron was without

indicators.note: without here means outside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: David Cameron, the former Prime Minister, was educated at Eton College

indicators.note: at the outset means the opening letter of the word support

explanation.surface: A political jab: national support was something Cameron lacked from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking: ETONIAN goes round S, the first letter of support. Eton is the elite school David Cameron attended.
explanation.definitionFit: A national is a citizen of a country, here one from the Baltic state of Estonia.

clue.text: Negotiated two road blocks when approaching

indicators.note: negotiated means worked around, so the letters of two are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: blocks means obstructs, sitting in the way inside the other piece

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A driver weaves around two road blocks on the way somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Negotiated' is the anagram signal and 'blocks' means sits inside. 'when' looks like a link word but supplies letters, leaving 'approaching' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Towards and approaching both describe movement in the direction of something.

clue.text: 'Brilliant company' — boy received praise

indicators.note: received means taken in, so one piece holds the others

parts.note: ace means brilliant, excellent
a boy is a lad

explanation.surface: A boy is praised for being in brilliant company.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around 'Brilliant company' are only surface; 'received' means the outer piece takes in the other two.
explanation.definitionFit: An accolade is an award or expression of praise and honour.

clue.text: Rider starts to holler at Gran, 'Pull over!'

indicators.note: starts to means the first letters of the next three words
over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to pull is to drag

explanation.surface: A cyclist or horse rider is told to pull over after shouting at a grandmother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes H, A, G; 'over' turns DRAG back to GARD. H. Rider Haggard wrote King Solomon's Mines.
explanation.definitionFit: H. Rider Haggard was the Victorian adventure novelist, so the definition names him by his middle name.

clue.text: PE teacher gets disciplined over a picture

indicators.note: disciplined means knocked into shape, so these letters are put into order

explanation.surface: A school PE teacher gets told off over a photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of PE TEACHER GETS plus A, shuffled as 'disciplined' signals, give the film title.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture is a film, and this is the 1963 war film about a mass breakout from a prison camp.

clue.text: Boobs on Page Three (Ariana's) regularly touched up

indicators.note: touched up means altered, so the chosen letters are rearranged
regularly means taking every other letter, starting from the first

explanation.surface: Newspaper Page Three photos of a model called Ariana have been airbrushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes T, R, E, R, A, A from THREE ARIANAS; 'touched up' rearranges them. Page Three was the Sun's topless-model feature.
explanation.definitionFit: Boobs means mistakes, and errata is the list of printed mistakes in a book.

clue.text: Meat product horse? Look into it

indicators.note: into means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: a pony is a small horse
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: A worried shopper wonders if a meat product contains horse and resolves to investigate.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the 2013 horsemeat scandal; 'into' signals one piece going inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Polony is a kind of sausage of finely ground cooked meat.

clue.text: Dress daring if unbecoming

indicators.note: to dress is to arrange, so these letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: A daring outfit that might be unflattering on its wearer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress' is the signal, rearranging DARING IF.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beneath one's dignity, from the Latin for below dignity, is unbecoming.

clue.text: Hunter on screen captures one divinely

indicators.note: captures means holds, so the second piece goes inside

parts.note: Holly Hunter is an American film actress
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A film hunter on screen catches someone in a heavenly way.
explanation.walkthrough: Holly Hunter won an Oscar for The Piano; 'captures' puts I inside her first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in a sacred or godly manner is behaving divinely.

clue.text: Turner leaves with instruction to follow

indicators.note: leaves means goes out, so the named letter is removed

parts.note: a wheel is something that turns

explanation.surface: The painter Turner departs, leaving behind directions for someone to come after him.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner looks like the painter but is just something that turns; 'leaves' removes W, short for with.
explanation.definitionFit: A command given to a dog, telling it to walk close behind its owner.

clue.text: Angers beats Rouen for a popular retirement venue

indicators.note: angers means riles up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: French football: Angers defeats Rouen, a match result between two French cities.
explanation.walkthrough: Angers looks like another French city name but is the verb, signalling an anagram of BEATS ROUEN. Eastbourne is a seaside town in Sussex popular with retirees.
explanation.definitionFit: This south-coast English seaside town is famous for its large retired population.

clue.text: Assumes a bit of work's wanted in majority of clues

indicators.note: wanted means lacking, so that letter is missing

parts.note: in this puzzle the down clues outnumber the across clues fourteen to twelve

indicators.note: a bit of means just the first letter of the word work

explanation.surface: Someone takes on a little work that is needed in most clues.
explanation.walkthrough: A self-referential clue: this grid has fourteen down clues to twelve across, so most clues are DOWNS; 'wanted' (lacking) removes W.
explanation.definitionFit: To don clothing is to put it on, and to assume a garment or role means the same.
